rules.statement: Apply the project-level build-scroll-3d-product-story skill to the existing docs/experiment car GLB route and deliver an actual enterprise product story rather than a technical loader demo.
Keep car-specific node selectors, group labels, offsets, assembly windows, camera, rotation, stage content, and CTA in docs/experiment/product-story.json; keep the runtime generic.
Control non-overlapping top-level assembly roots so parent and descendant transforms are not double-applied; keep BodyUnderside as the stationary product foundation.
Use model node names as evidence for business-readable groups, but do not claim a production powertrain, manufacturing sequence, or engineering fact that the concept GLB does not establish.
Deliver intro, exploded structure, semantic assembly, complete-product reveal, and final hero states synchronized from one normalized scroll progress; ROKE remains a narrative reference only.
Derive every controlled transform from captured base transforms, the approved manifest, and normalized progress so forward and reverse scrolling produce the same pose without drift.

Render on loading, scroll target changes, finite interpolation, resize, or explicit finite motion and stop after settling; do not retain an idle permanent requestAnimationFrame loop or setAnimationLoop.
Preserve the existing Draco geometry, KTX2/BasisU textures, single-GLB delivery, model attribution, and CC BY 4.0 license notice.
Keep loading, WebGL failure, poster-capable fallback, and reduced-motion behavior; reduced motion resolves directly to the final assembled hero state.

Record browser identity, 1440x900 viewport, device pixel ratio, cache state, first usable product frame, p50 and p95 animation frame time, frames over 16.7 and 33.3 ms, Long Animation Frames when supported, main-thread timing when supported, memory when supported, and idle renders after settling.

On the declared local desktop browser run, require frame-time p50 no greater than 18.5 ms, p95 no greater than 25 ms, frames over 33.3 ms no more than 2 percent, and zero renderer frames during the post-settle idle observation window.
Keep raw asset bytes and request counts separate from runtime frame evidence; do not use a fixed 4 Mbps weak-network gate or infer GPU performance from file size.
Deliver through the configured main:/docs GitHub Pages source, confirm the public experiment route returns HTTP 200, and recheck the consumer-visible page after deployment.
